question_answered: What can be established authoritatively about a Hiland T5502 transmitter, which hardware and regional variants or documentation conflicts exist, and which non-destructive observations are needed before judging compatibility?
applicability_to_t5502_hcs301: Direct for the Hiland-branded T5502 product identity and advertised 433.92 MHz, three-channel, rolling-code characteristics. Conditional for the claimed HCS301/HC301 encoder: Hiland's public T5502 page and 2023-2024 catalogue do not identify the encoder IC, so the requester's IC observation must be confirmed from a sharp package photograph. 'HC301' may be an incomplete reading, a house-marked or compatible part, or an HCS301, and the enclosure model alone does not prove the cryptographic provisioning domain.
authorization_assumption: The transmitter and controlled installation are owned by the requester or the requester has explicit authority from the owner/administrator. Opening, photographing, testing, enrolling, deleting, or replacing credentials must remain within that authority.
key_findings: Fact (manufacturer): Hiland currently describes T5502 as a three-channel, 433.92 MHz rolling-code transmitter with a 12 V 23A battery and a nominal 50 m indoor working distance.
Fact (manufacturer catalogue): Hiland's 2023-2024 catalogue likewise lists 433.92 MHz, three channels, rolling code, and a 12 V 23A battery, but gives 69 x 39 x 16 mm and 32 g.

Conflict: Hiland's current family/product presentation gives a 59 x 33 x 16 mm size, while the catalogue gives 69 x 39 x 16 mm; an Australian specialist reseller gives approximately 58 x 32 x 15 mm. This is consistent with a documentation error, measurement convention difference, or enclosure revision, but the source set does not resolve which.

Conflict: the authoritative Hiland product page and catalogue specify a 12 V 23A battery, whereas a Peruvian dealer says 3 V CR2032 and a Made-in-China supplier listing says 3 V lithium. Battery type therefore must be read from the installed cell and holder, not inferred from 'T5502' alone.

Fact (manufacturer): Hiland documents a self-learning procedure for some receivers that uses an already learned transmitter and then causes the receiver to learn the new transmitter. This can avoid opening the receiver enclosure, but it is still active receiver participation and is not transmitter-to-transmitter cryptographic copying.

Fact (Microchip, if the IC is genuinely HCS301): HCS301 is an 8-lead PDIP or SOIC code-hopping encoder operating from 3.5 V to 13 V, with a 66-bit word comprising a 32-bit hopping portion and 34-bit fixed portion. Its package marking example includes 'HCS301' plus date/lot or customer-specific codes.

Inference: A clear HCS301 top mark supports encoder-family identification, but neither that mark nor a matching RF frequency establishes that two transmitters share Hiland's provisioning/key domain or will be accepted by a particular receiver.

Safe conclusion: The best non-destructive identity packet is photos of front/back enclosure labels, battery and polarity markings, both PCB faces and silkscreen revision, the encoder top mark, and the frequency-setting component, plus a receive-only measurement of center frequency and modulation/timing. Do not expose or attempt to recover secret EEPROM contents.

Microchip Technology, 'HCS301 KEELOQ Code Hopping Encoder,' DS21143C, June 2011, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/21143C.pdf (accessed 2026-10-01).
Microchip Technology, HCS301 product page (status shown as In Production when indexed), https://www.microchip.com/en-us/product/HCS301 (accessed 2026-10-01).
secondary_sources: Reids Remotes, 'Hiland T5502 - 3 button black rolling code remote control,' https://www.reidsremotes.com.au/home/2748-hiland-t5502-3-button-black-rolling-code-remote-control.html (accessed 2026-10-01). Specialist reseller; useful for receiver and cross-model claims, dimensions, and 23AE battery, but not the OEM specification authority.

Mayer Peru, 'Control Remoto Hiland Modelo T5502,' https://mayer.pe/accesorios-y-repuestos/control-remoto-hiland-modelo-t5502 (accessed 2026-10-01). Dealer claim of CR2032/3 V; conflicts with Hiland and requires unit-level verification.

Made-in-China supplier page attributed to Zhejiang Hiland, 'Hiland High Quality Transmitter T5502,' https://hiland.en.made-in-china.com/product/bxFUPNsoLqcY/China-Hiland-High-Quality-Transmitter-T5502-with-433-92MHz-Frequency.html (accessed 2026-10-01). Marketplace/supplier listing; its 3 V lithium claim conflicts with Hiland's own page.
evidence_quality: High for the currently advertised Hiland model, frequency, channel count, rolling-code designation, and manufacturer-described self-learning behavior because those come from Hiland. High for HCS301 electrical, package, and protocol characteristics because they come from Microchip's datasheet. Moderate-to-low for PCB codes, cross-model interchangeability, receiver capacity, dimensions, and 3 V variants because available support is reseller or conflicting catalogue evidence. No authoritative teardown in the reviewed sources proves that every T5502 revision contains an HCS301, identifies the RF resonator marking, or establishes a universal Hiland manufacturer-key domain.
source_dates: Microchip DS21143C: Revision C, June 2011. Hiland catalogue: labelled 2023-2024. Hiland current product page and all current web pages retrieved 2026-10-01. Reseller publication dates were not stated [uncertain].
source_claim_type: Hiland product specifications and enrollment instructions: manufacturer documentation. Hiland catalogue: manufacturer catalogue. HCS301 architecture and markings: semiconductor manufacturer datasheet. Reids Remotes, Mayer, and Made-in-China: dealer/reseller statements. Any conclusion that the requester's 'HC301' is an HCS301 or that differing dimensions/batteries represent hardware revisions is inference pending photographs.
relevant_components: T5502 enclosure and three switches; installed battery and holder; transmitter PCB and its silkscreen/revision; 8-pin encoder reportedly marked HC301/HCS301; RF oscillator/transistor stage; frequency-setting resonator or equivalent; antenna trace; status LED; and the external receiver/decoder with its firmware, learned-credential memory, and Hiland/OEM provisioning configuration. HCS301 itself generates baseband PWM data; external RF circuitry determines the carrier implementation.
hardware_revision_and_markings: Record the exact text/logo/model and regulatory marks on both enclosure halves; installed cell designation, voltage, polarity, and holder geometry; PCB manufacturer/model/revision codes on both faces; encoder package style and every top-mark line; all markings on the SAW resonator/crystal and RF transistor; switch count and wiring; and any rebrand label. Microchip documents HCS301 in 8-lead PDIP and SOIC, with example package marking 'HCS301' plus year/week, lot, and possibly customer-specific information. A PCB code can differ from the enclosure label in rebranded products; Reids gives an example of a differently branded enclosure whose board says Hiland T6402, so board identity should be captured independently.
power_variant: Best-supported T5502 specification is one 12 V type-23A alkaline cell (also marketed as A23/23AE). Hiland's current page and catalogue agree. Conflicting dealer/marketplace pages claim a 3 V CR2032 or unspecified 3 V lithium version [uncertain]. HCS301 supports 3.5-13 V, so a genuine single-cell 3 V design would require a different encoder, boost arrangement, atypical operation, or erroneous listing; inspect the actual holder and cell before powering or buying a replacement.
rf_profile: Hiland specifies 433.92 MHz. The reviewed official sources do not state RF modulation explicitly [uncertain]; HCS301 supplies a PWM data output to external RF circuitry, and common implementations key an RF carrier, but the unit's modulation, occupied bandwidth, symbol timing selection, frequency error, and radiated level should be established only by receive-only measurement. Frequency match alone is insufficient because message format, key derivation, enrollment policy, and receiver firmware must also match.
observable_data: Without transmitting or opening the receiver, an owner may document enclosure/label identity, installed battery, board and component markings, dimensions, button behavior, and LED behavior. Receive-only capture of the owned transmitter can establish center frequency, likely modulation family, timing, repetition pattern, fixed serial-number-bearing fields, button/status variation, and whether successive presses change. It cannot by itself prove the hidden crypt key, receiver-stored state, manufacturer code, or acceptance by a specific decoder. Avoid unnecessary button presses because each normal operation advances transmitter state.
protected_or_secret_data: For a genuine HCS301, the unique 64-bit crypt key, EEPROM configuration, synchronization state, any secure-learning seed, and the receiver/OEM manufacturer-code or key-generation domain are security-sensitive. Microchip states that encoder EEPROM is not accessible through an external connection and is read-protected; this report provides no values or recovery procedure.
manufacturer_key_domain_evidence: Non-secret evidence should include an explicit Hiland or authorized-distributor compatibility statement naming both transmitter and receiver models; receiver manual/model/firmware identity; genuine replacement part number; documented enrollment procedure; and, ideally, written OEM confirmation that the replacement is provisioned for that receiver family. Similar enclosure, HCS301 marking, 433.92 MHz carrier, serial format, or reseller use of 'universal' is not sufficient evidence of a shared OEM provisioning domain.
compatibility_constraints: Carrier frequency and regional approval; modulation and data timing; HCS301-compatible framing if applicable; OEM key-generation/manufacturer-code domain; receiver learning strategy and firmware; available receiver credential slots; channel/button mapping; synchronization policy; battery/electrical revision; and whether remote self-learning is enabled. A product advertised as HCS301 or KeeLoq compatible may still be cryptographically incompatible or require receiver enrollment.
variant_conflicts: Documented conflicts are 12 V 23A versus 3 V/CR2032 battery, 69 x 39 x 16 mm versus about 59 x 33 x 16 mm dimensions, and enclosure label versus possible different PCB model/rebrand. Resolve safely by examining the actual unit, comparing official photographs and board codes, making receive-only measurements, and asking Hiland or an authorized distributor with photographs and receiver model. Do not infer electrical compatibility from enclosure resemblance.
access_assumption: Four cases must be separated: (1) no transmitter enclosure access still permits label photography and receive-only RF characterization; (2) transmitter enclosure access permits battery/PCB/IC photography but not secret recovery; (3) no physical receiver-enclosure access may still permit Hiland's over-the-air self-learning on supported receivers; (4) no receiver participation at all excludes both learn-button and remote-triggered learning. Lack of RF reach additionally prevents any over-the-air enrollment or acceptance test.
receiver_dependency: Identity research itself does not require receiver participation. Producing a usable additional credential normally does: Hiland's documented self-learning explicitly causes a supported receiver to enter learning and accept a new transmitter, or an installer uses the receiver's learn interface. A genuine OEM-provisioned replacement may share protocol/key-domain compatibility but still needs learning unless that receiver's documented policy says otherwise.
receiver_make_model_firmware: Unknown [uncertain]. Establish it from the motor/controller invoice, exterior label photographed without defeating safety covers, owner/installer records, or an authorized technician. Record receiver model, PCB revision, firmware/version if exposed in normal administration, radio module model, supported transmitter list, and manual revision.
physical_access_vs_receiver_participatio: Hiland says some receivers can be placed into learning by an already learned transmitter, so receiver enclosure access may be unnecessary. The receiver still actively participates over the air and modifies its credential memory. With neither physical access nor any receiver participation, unit identification can proceed but supported enrollment cannot be completed.
existing_authorized_remote_required: Yes for Hiland's documented remote self-learning path; not necessarily for receiver learn-button or authorized installer/OEM service paths.
enrollment_method_and_authority: Use only the procedure in the exact receiver manual. For supported Hiland receivers, the owner/administrator may invoke documented self-learning with an already enrolled master/old transmitter; otherwise an authorized person or installer uses the receiver's learn function. OEM/dealer provisioning should be requested with proof of ownership. Do not treat transmitter copying claims as a substitute for receiver-authorized enrollment.
credential_semantics: A supported replacement should be a unique, newly enrolled credential or a genuine vendor-provisioned compatible transmitter, not a byte-for-byte duplicate. Remote self-learning is enrollment into the receiver even though it begins from an existing remote. A claim of 'clone' based only on captured transmissions is unsubstantiated for rolling code.
receiver_memory_and_revocation: Model-dependent and unknown until the receiver is identified [uncertain]. A specialist reseller claims Hiland R5101/R5102 support up to 30 remotes and R5103/R5104 up to 300, but this is secondary evidence and does not establish the requester's receiver. Determine whether learning appends, overwrites, or clears memory; revoke lost transmitters; preserve an inventory; and avoid any all-memory reset without a recovery plan.
legitimate_routes: Buy a genuine T5502 or explicitly approved successor from Hiland/authorized distributor and enroll it using the exact receiver manual.
Where the receiver supports it, use Hiland's documented self-learning path with a currently enrolled authorized transmitter; this avoids opening the receiver but not receiver participation.
Ask an authorized installer or OEM to identify the receiver, supply a correctly provisioned transmitter, enroll it, and audit/revoke lost credentials.
If the legacy receiver is unsupported or its key domain cannot be verified, install a documented replacement receiver/radio module and issue new unique remotes under owner control.
prerequisites: Proof of ownership/authorization; photographs and markings from the actual T5502; actual battery type; receive-only frequency confirmation; receiver make/model/manual; a free credential slot; and either an existing authorized transmitter for supported self-learning or authorized receiver/installer access.
equipment_or_service_needed: Camera or macro-capable phone, calipers, battery tester, and optionally a spectrum analyzer or receive-only SDR/frequency counter used without transmitting. For provisioning, a genuine replacement and authorized installer/OEM support may be needed. No key-extraction or attack tooling is required or recommended.
expected_outcomes: Identification yields a defensible model/revision dossier and a compatibility shortlist. OEM/installer enrollment yields a distinct working credential. Receiver migration yields a new managed credential domain. None of these safe routes promises a cryptographic duplicate of the existing transmitter.
limitations: Public Hiland material does not identify the T5502 encoder IC, PCB revisions, modulation, key-domain identifier, or every compatible receiver. Conflicting battery and dimension listings reduce confidence in variant identity. Self-learning applies only to some receivers and requires an existing enrolled transmitter. Availability and regional approvals may vary.
cost_or_effort_band: Identity documentation and receive-only testing: low. Genuine replacement plus self-enrollment: low to medium. Installer identification/enrollment: medium. Receiver/radio migration with re-enrollment: medium to high. Actual prices and availability are region-dependent [uncertain].
route_classification: Device identification supporting replacement, authorized enrollment, vendor provisioning, interoperability verification, or receiver migration. Independent cryptographic duplication without receiver participation is unsupported.
product_status_and_authenticity: Hiland lists T5502 on its current manufacturer site, but retail availability, region, and exact revision are uncertain. Prefer Hiland or traceable authorized sellers, obtain photographs of the exact stock, verify battery/revision and return policy, and avoid generic 'copy' remotes whose provisioning domain is undocumented. Microchip currently indexes HCS301 as In Production, but a chip marking alone does not authenticate the complete remote.
feasibility_without_receiver: Without physical receiver access but with receiver RF reach, an additional genuine transmitter may be feasible through Hiland's documented self-learning on some receivers, provided an enrolled authorized transmitter is available. Without any receiver participation, public observations of a T5502/HCS301 do not establish a supported way to create an independently accepted credential; identification and purchase can proceed, but enrollment/acceptance cannot be completed. OEM service based on installation records is the only plausible no-local-receiver-contact route and remains receiver-/vendor-policy dependent [uncertain].
confidence: High that the canonical current Hiland T5502 is advertised as 433.92 MHz, three-channel, rolling code, and 12 V 23A, and high that an HCS301 marking has the documented Microchip architecture. Moderate for the exact physical revision because official dimensions conflict and non-OEM listings claim a different battery. Low until inspected for the assertion that this specific unit's 'HC301' is a genuine HCS301 and belongs to a particular Hiland key domain.
legal_or_authorization_notes: Radio reception, device opening, credential enrollment, and access-control testing can be regulated differently by jurisdiction and may affect warranties or tenancy/HOA rules. Test only owned/authorized equipment, do not intercept third-party traffic, and obtain installer or legal advice where ownership, shared premises, radio compliance, or access authority is disputed.
operational_risks: Repeated transmitter testing advances the rolling counter and excessive off-site presses may require resynchronization. Incorrect battery voltage or polarity can damage the unit. Opening may damage clips, expose a coin/alkaline cell hazard, or erase provenance markings. Incorrect learn/reset sequences may erase remotes, consume the last slot, change channel behavior, or lock users out. Unsupervised gate/door activation presents crushing and property risks.
enrollment_side_effects: Learning changes receiver memory. Depending on receiver firmware it may append, overwrite, evict, or clear credentials; exact behavior is unknown until the receiver manual is identified. Existing remotes should be inventoried and tested afterward, and lost credentials should be revoked where supported.
prohibited_actionable_details_omitted: Yes. Key or seed extraction, cryptographic attack, rolling-code defeat, replay, brute force, EEPROM bypass, and unauthorized-access instructions are omitted.
stop_conditions: Stop if the receiver or transmitter identity remains ambiguous; the battery marking conflicts with the planned supply; the enclosure is shared, leased, safety-critical, or not clearly authorized; a procedure may erase all receiver memory; no backup authorized remote exists; unexpected gate/door motion occurs; the receiver reaches capacity; or an exact OEM manual cannot be obtained. Hand off to Hiland, an authorized installer/locksmith, or legal counsel as appropriate.
recommended_next_steps: Create a photo set of the remote exterior, label, battery and holder, PCB faces, IC top mark, RF resonator marking, and PCB revision; redact personal/site identifiers before sharing publicly.
Confirm whether the marking is HCS301, HC301, or another device and whether the installed cell is 12 V 23A or a coin cell; do not power it from a guessed voltage.
Measure only the owned transmitter's carrier and basic timing with receive-only equipment and minimize button presses.
Identify the receiver from records or a safe exterior label and obtain its exact manual and supported transmitter list.

Ask Hiland or a traceable distributor to confirm the T5502 revision, genuine replacement part, receiver compatibility, and whether remote self-learning is supported; then perform supervised authorized enrollment and acceptance testing.
questions_for_owner_or_vendor: What exact text appears on the enclosure, PCB silkscreen, encoder, RF resonator, and installed battery?
Is the receiver a Hiland R5101/R5102/R5103/R5104 or another controller, and what PCB/firmware revision does it have?
Does its official manual support remote-triggered self-learning, and which already enrolled transmitter is designated as master?
Does learning append one credential or erase/overwrite existing credentials, and how many slots remain?
Is this replacement factory-provisioned for the same OEM domain and regional frequency, and is that compatibility guaranteed in writing?
What warranty, authenticity evidence, and return right apply if enrollment fails?
rollback_and_acceptance_test: Before enrollment, inventory every authorized remote/channel and preserve the old transmitter unchanged. Confirm the gate/door safety zone is clear and have a manual release/administrator present. Enroll only one candidate using the exact receiver manual. Test each new and existing remote once per assigned channel from a safe location, verify no unintended channel operates, verify stop/safety devices, and check that a previously lost/revoked remote remains rejected. If any existing credential fails or memory behavior differs from the manual, stop; use the documented receiver backup/restore or authorized installer process rather than experimenting with reset sequences.
